subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: What trust boundary and default activation policy should OpenClaw enforce for plugin, agent, or external recurring cron jobs that can spend model quota?
rationale: The fix changes cron defaults, plugin scheduling contracts, provider/model spend policy, persisted upgrade behavior, and security posture, so automation cannot choose the default safely.

options.title: Provenance-gated scheduling API
options.body: Create or harden a scheduling path that records gateway-injected origin, requires approval or disabled-by-default activation for non-operator recurring jobs, and requires explicit model/cost policy before execution.

options.title: Default external jobs disabled
options.body: Make plugin, agent, and external recurring cron registrations inactive until the operator enables them, accepting a compatibility migration and UX cost for existing automation.

options.title: Keep auto-enable with spend guards
options.body: Preserve current activation behavior but add budget/quota warnings and circuit breakers, leaving consent and provenance weaker than the issue requests.

recommendation.title: Provenance-gated scheduling API
recommendation.body: Create or harden a scheduling path that records gateway-injected origin, requires approval or disabled-by-default activation for non-operator recurring jobs, and requires explicit model/cost policy before execution.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is the strongest current implementation-surface signal from recent cron/task/model-selection history, while the decision should still include security/product reviewers.
